subject: convergence failure of otherwise good model

messages.author: caaac2dc0aae28b8
messages.subject: convergence failure of otherwise good model
parts:
I have a question about how to proceed with an analysis in which there is=
=20
a convergence failure for a model that otherwise looks like the best mode=
l=20
for the detection function. This is an analysis of an aerial survey of=20=

bottlenose dolphins in a shallow lagoon system in Florida. Following dat=
a=20
screening, I decided on analysis of ungrouped data with data truncated at=
=20
273 m (9.3% observations, original data range 0-736 m). I tried six=20
models for the detection function (Half-normal Key with both cosine and=20=

hermite polynomial, Uniform key with both simple polynomial and cosine,=20=

and hazard-rate key with both simple polynomial and cosine). The Uniform=
=20
key with simple polynomial series expansion and 1 adjustment terms had th=
e=20
lowest AIC. The next best model was Uniform, cosine (AIC=3D3.64), then H=
alf-
normal cosine (AIC=3D6.49). However, the Uniform/simple model with 1=20
adjustment term failed to converge, but was still selected as the best=20=

model.=20=20

Looking at the iteration history for this model, I see that by the sevent=
h=20
iteration, the likelihood stays very close to -1250 and the estimate of A=

(1) stays very close to -1.07. I tried setting the starting value near=20=

where the convergence left off, but after many attempts, I was not able t=
o=20
get it to converge.=20=20

I next tried fitting the same models to the data grouped into six=20
intervals. Again, the Uniform, simple polynomial (with 1 adjustment term)=
=20
was the best model, and this time the model converged. However, the=20
detection function was slightly different between the two analyses: {f(0)=

ungrouped =3D 0.00569 vs. f(0)grouped =3D 0.00533; A(1)ungrouped =3D -1.0=
74 vs. A
(1)grouped =3D -0.938}. The precision for the grouped data was lower=20
(CVungrouped =3D 10.0%, CVgrouped =3D 10.5%), and the density estimates w=
ere=20
slightly different (ungrouped =3D 0.0050194, grouped =3D 0.0046979).=20=20=


This analysis is of one geographic strata within a larger analysis=20
comprised of four geographic strata. I have decided on using separate=20=

detection function models between geographic strata, based on comparison=20=

of the AIC of pooled verses separate data. I=92d like to use the ungroup=
ed=20
data in this geographic strata, to be consistent with how the other=20
geographic starta are being treated. Although the is a moderate amount o=
f=20
heaping in the data (due to use of an inclinometer to measure angles from=
=20
the survey aircraft which were later converted into perpendicular=20
distances), the analyses of ungrouped data have performed very well for=20=

the other three geographic strata.

To refocus on my questions, I=92m wondering if I can I trusted the parame=
ter=20
estimates of the model that failed to converge, or should I use the=20
grouped data analysis? Or is there another way to proceed?

--
